title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes the argument begun on the previous page.

**Setting (previous page).** Let k = F_q. Take E a supersingular elliptic curve over k whose endomorphisms are all defined over k. Put G_0 = Ê, the formal group of E: it is one-dimensional of height 2, Manin's G_{1,1}. Then End(G_0) ≅ End(E) ⊗ Z_p = 𝒜, the maximal order in the quaternion division algebra over Q_p.

**Twisting.** Forms of G_0 over k are classified by continuous 1-cocycles of Gal(k̄/k) ≅ Ẑ with values in Aut(G_0) = 𝒜^*. Such a cocycle is determined by the image θ of the Frobenius generator, and since 𝒜^* is profinite any θ ∈ 𝒜^* is allowed. The twisted form G' has Frobenius endomorphism φ' = θφ.

**Obstruction.** Suppose G' (possibly after a finite extension of k) is a formal subgroup of Â for an abelian variety A over k. Then φ' is the restriction of the Frobenius of A. The characteristic polynomial of φ' on the Dieudonné module of G' then divides the Weil polynomial of A, which has integer coefficients. So det φ' (the reduced norm) must be an algebraic number all of whose conjugates have the same absolute value. Since the end-of-page fact below requires φ central in End(G_0), with φ² = ±q in Z and E's endomorphisms defined over k, det φ is ±q to a power. Hence det θ = Nrd(θ) would have to be algebraic, with all conjugates of absolute value 1.

**This page.** "Mais bien entendu il est facile de trouver θ unité de 𝒜 tel que det θ ne soit pas algébrique..." Indeed, Nrd: 𝒜^* → Z_p^* is surjective. So one can choose θ with Nrd θ transcendental over Q, which is possible since Z_p^* is uncountable. Then G' is a form of G_{1,1} over k that cannot be realised inside the formal group of any abelian variety, even after a finite extension of k: for that extension, π'^n = θ^n π^n has transcendental reduced norm.

**Context.** This is a remark in Grothendieck's post-1970 notes on Barsotti–Tate groups, attached to the 1966 Tate letter on crystals. The next page turns to infinitesimal extensions of BT groups and the infinitesimal structure of modular schemes, i.e. the Montreal 1970 / Serre–Tate circle.
errors: No mathematical error. Two implicit points: (i) the twisted Frobenius is θφ (or θ^{-1}φ depending on convention), which does not affect the argument; (ii) the passage to a finite extension needs φ central, which holds because the endomorphisms of E are defined over k, as noted on the previous page. The machine transcription's 'nilpotent' should be 'algébrique' for the argument to make sense.

ideas.what: Forms of a one-dimensional height-2 formal group (G_{1,1}) over a finite field, obtained by twisting Frobenius by a unit of the quaternion order, need not embed in the formal group of any abelian variety, even after a finite extension; the obstruction is that the Frobenius eigenvalues must be Weil numbers.
ideas.modern_name: Non-algebraizability of p-divisible / formal groups over finite fields (Frobenius not a Weil number); Honda–Tate / Dieudonné-module constraints
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore following Weil, Tate (1966), Honda (1968), Manin (1963)
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed around Grothendieck's Montréal 1970 lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974); unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short, correct and essentially folklore remark: one picks a quaternion unit with transcendental reduced norm, so the twisted Frobenius cannot be a Weil number. It completes the previous page's counterexample and contains nothing beyond standard Honda–Tate/Dieudonné reasoning.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 first words: likely 'unité de 𝒜' (the quaternion order 𝒜 from the previous page), not 'construit[?] de A'.
Line 3 last word: likely 'algébrique', not 'nilpotent[?]' — the statement is 'det Θ ne soit pas algébrique'.
The struck-out phrase in line 2 is '[-ne satisfaisant pas-]', correctly identified; the circled Θ in brown at the end of line 1 is θ, the twisting automorphism.
